summary: Assess decision authority, partner risk, and community influence with practical localisation tools. Explore the five-day advanced course.
lede: Locally led development means local actors shape priorities and decisions affecting their communities. This training is for programme leaders, partnership managers and localisation advisers assessing whether that influence is reflected in programme governance. Participants map decision rights, test commitments against evidence, and review community accountability, funding and risk allocation to develop governance and reporting action plans.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who can influence programme governance and need to examine whether local actors shape real decisions, not only programme language.
modules: Grand Bargain Progress and Executive Reporting
prerequisites: Advanced-level course. You should have experience designing, managing, funding, or overseeing humanitarian or development programmes and working with local partner agreements, budgets, or programme decisions. No coding or programming is required.
